items.note: S4.1 states the signed exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with all scratch restored. The sub-steps follow the proof at 741-765 (net change (JV+RG)x independent of a,c; bit coefficient |S cap T| mod 2 and complex coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2; the three stages (x,y+x),(-y,y+x),(-y,x)) and give the neighbour and wire counts of 767-782.

Gives the invariant that the stored array equals D_v applied to the logical array, its passage through edges and through gates because a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, the operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and the per-route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, exactly as at 804-825.

Covers the bilinear spaces, the terminal labels, the stage transitions, the gate-label table eq:motif-labels, the 2->5 nesting from t_X perp t_Y, the single decreasing edge 3->4 (loss h, so L=Ich), telescoping to Wm-2N+2L, orthonormal bases over F_2 and L/N=100/539, 101/539. It does not reproduce the full residual table, but its method names that tabulation. The S4.3 headline garbles 'L/N below 1/2' as 'L ... is L_b/N ... below N/2'; the substance is right.

States the projection assignment with -P_{U_a} at X_a sources, the endpoint identity, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m. It derives them by the paper's route: rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one, and the endpoint check P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m.

Follows the proof step by step: weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal vectors, the q_V-q_U formula, the character-to-translation identity giving aI+bX_v, the s_c count with deficit 2N-2L_c, the X_a->Y_a pair with 27 inverse factors fixed by C=iZC^{-1}Z, and C^{otimes m} (or C^{otimes mk} on k columns) on every role.

Gives L<N/2, both strict inequalities s<Wm with their exact values, the deficits eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500 above 20*2^{-50}, log m<20, and the bound m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta). Hence tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, as at 1319-1346.

S2 and S3 are infer steps that state both lemmas faithfully: digit permutation, digit move, split and merge, and cyclic row split into W streams; the controlled shift mod Q and unit scalings. S3 names the split-and-merge idea, but neither step has sub-steps following the proofs. The b^{O(1)} offset condition appears only in S3's quote.

Gives A=E_1 Pi E_2 by top-row, rightmost-pivot elimination, the odd prime avoiding denominators and diagonal numerators, triangular updates in descending physical order as controlled shifts, and the three-step realisation of H_i+=D_j with one interchange. Hence exactly a interchanges plus O(V), matching 1375-1446.

Follows the proof: cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} on each edge by recursive interchanges, the frame identity giving H<-H+D on every row, the three shears for the interchange, s calls, the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solved by the geometric sum, and the fixed-tape parking-stack schedule with the descriptor bound.

Reproduces k and rho, the field-order display that builds a row field R=q^{2 rho}>=W^k, row padding to R'<2R, the base-m pieces with cost O(V) sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau), padding of binary ranges to [q^e], and the one-bit-difference case.

Gives the basic identities, conjugation by P_M with M in GL(m,F_2), the m slots of f chunks with one child (C^{eps})^{otimes f} per residual vector, the inverse-child identity, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{otimes D}=b^D S_D C^{otimes D} S_D.

Follows the proof closely: the eight conditional updates and their cycles, the guard decomposition, each line as one cyclic shift, the bad set with delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting only B, the swap-rotate-unswap implementation, radix-sort repair, the full cost and its simplification, and the application to a change of basis. 'Moves by at most eight' is the paper's weaker usable bound; the paper shows four.

Gives q_0 and k_0, the row index from the first q_0 chunks, the role split with child volume V/W, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e), the internal-node bound O(e^lambda), the leaf bound O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and the base-m sum O(d^{lambda'}). S4.6.3.2 wrongly folds the s children into the node overhead (listed under errors), but S4.6.3.7 states the recurrence correctly.

States Q_p(Hz) in O(Vd^{lambda'}) with error <sqrt2 2^{-p} and one final truncation. Derives the guard width Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) from A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E (constants E, B, nu=11, C_1=20, C_0=128mB^2) and checks the packed-call terms over the parameter bands (R_g, A_*<=C_A p, both extra terms o(1)), as at 2686-2757.

Gives character cancellation and F^+F^-=I/t, decimation in frequency into bit-reversed order, B_tF_t^- and F_t^+B_t^{-1}, grouped rounds H then J_E, and the layout L. The costs dK, pK^{tau-1} and l d^{lambda'}, the commutation of J_E with Q_p, and the error sqrt2 l 2^{-p} follow 2990-3199. S5.2's method misorders the prefix-slot rounds (listed under errors); the sub-steps are otherwise faithful.

Gives B_0=2^{4p} evaluation, the separation bound |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, two's-complement block encoding, centered-residue extraction with the residual identity, negacyclic reduction, the final shift by p+l, and four O(rp)-bit products, all as at 3233-3367.

Gives the definition and contraction of M_r, the retained LB order with P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the normalization by M, the error chain 2delta+eta, 3delta+eta and then M(3delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, and the total cost, matching the proof at 3414-3494.

Follows the proof: the maps S and T, the N=CTD Neumann inverse, the normalizations S', J', D' with product 2^{-2alpha^2}, A and B_0, the quoted numerical maps and errors, the ordered selection C, the tensor identity with gamma=2d alpha^2, linewise error dp^2, cost and axis exposure O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)).

Gives the periodicity of a, the coefficient comparison leaving exp(2pi i sum s_i j_i k_i/t_i), Q reading frequency -s_i j_i, F^+_s R=R^{-1}F^+_s from substituting h=ck, and the cancellation to (u*v)/S^2, as at 3938-3987.

Gives all fixed exponents and sizes, alpha, gamma and eta, the Rosser-Schoenfeld prime count via HvdH Lemma 5.1, distinct odd primes in ((1-2eta)t_i,(1-eta)t_i], T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i>p, and the n^{o(1)} trial-division search.

Gives Phi as an isomorphism (the image of x has order S), the triangular coordinate formula, padding insertion, updates in order i=d,...,1 as prefix-controlled rotations of the valid interval, and the O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)) axis reversal cost.

Gives the well-definedness (zeta y)^r=1, the diagonal isometric isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T and the computed version with approximate twist factors. The twist error below 4 appears in S8.7.2.

Gives the chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A=RF_s and its conjugate, input scaling by 2^{-b-2}, the six steps, and the roles of the two scales S. The S8 headline's 'O(Tp) steps beyond the layer costs' is inaccurate (listed under errors); S9 gives the correct costs.

Reproduces the error chain E_ring<5TL, the complex convolution <6TL, the chirp <8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, (2E_s+2), (3E_s+2), E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L and the final 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2. It also gives the disk margins, rounding to exact c_j<2^{3b}, and the carry recurrence with its invariant.

Reproduces all table rows with their powers, the margins g_1..g_7 with min g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, the per-row justifications, setup and exceptional-stream bounds o(V), absorption of log powers into p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff.

S1 names the Schonhage-Strassen n log n conjecture and the strict power saving. No step gives the eventual-lower-bound formulation or the liminf argument of 381-387 that turns the bound into a refutation.

errors.says: At a node with e=m^k chunks, the s children plus binary basis changes, scalar gates, endpoint corrections and reassembly cost O(V((eK)^tau+1)) at that node.
errors.paper: Only the non-recursive work (binary basis changes and their inverses, scalar gates, endpoint corrections, reassembly) costs O(V((eK)^tau+1)) at the node; the s children cost s(V/W)F(e/m) separately (2289-2296, 2410-2412).

errors.says: Method: run the first b+1<=K rounds on prefix slots bit by bit, then the remaining qK rounds with the fast simultaneous layer.
errors.paper: The prefix-slot rounds are not all first: the round h=l-1 on the long axes comes first, then the qK layer rounds on the chunks, and finally the b bottom rounds h=b-1,...,0 on prefix slots (3058-3063).

errors.says: The multiplication algorithm obtains the exact 2n-bit product in O(Tp) steps beyond the layer costs.
errors.paper: Besides the butterfly layers, the algorithm has several superlinear costs: chunk exchanges for the layout (pK^{tau-1}, the term that sets kappa), CRT and axis layouts (d^2(1+l^tau)), Gaussian line maps (dp^{1/2+delta} alpha), chirps (dp^delta) and packed products (log(rp)) per unit volume (4815-4831, 4857-4906). S9 states this correctly.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from start to finish. S4 builds the fixed exchange network, frames and nested labels, the two interfaces with s<Wm, and tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. These feed the interchange recurrence (S4.5) and the batched layer recurrence (S4.6). S5-S8 cover transforms, convolution, resampling, chirp cancellation, the algorithm and exact recovery, and S9 assembles the margins into kappa=2^{-182}. There is no break, only thin spots: a node-overhead step conflated with child calls (S4.6.3.2), the round order in S5.2's method, a loose cost claim in S8's headline, and the refutation clause of the conjecture, which is only mentioned.

steps.note: S4.1.1 gives h=100, v, N=v^3, m=h^3. S4.1.2 indexes the stages by coordinates of a in T^3. S4.1 and S4.1.9 give the fixed linear network sending (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoring every scratch wire.
A common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and each edge pays only D_v D_u^{-1}; the per-route operator is stated.
Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of F^{otimes3} of dimension m. Every edge joins comparable labels, and the only decreasing edges are the central 3->4 edges, each losing h.
rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested nondegenerate labels, with the N source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one as the only exceptions.
Sum of |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich by telescoping at gates; s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 are below 1/2. With the N extra source ranks a strict saving remains, giving s_b<W_b m (deficit N-2L_b implicit in the formula) and s_c<W_c m with deficit 2N-2L_c>0.
M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m with the X_a check P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m, so the network applies H<-H+D on every role, scratch rows included.
The rank-a shear factors as E_1 Pi E_2 and costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Each edge is implemented by recursive interchanges, so a node makes exactly s recursive calls.
Children have volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20, so F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: All nine steps are reconstructed with their defining content and in the paper's order: fixed network, frames, labels, rank equals dimension change, budget, strict saving L/N<1/2, endpoint identity, rank-many recursive calls, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The bit-case deficit N-2L_b>0 is left implicit in s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m; the paper states it explicitly.
